purpose: Typed-node annotation schema for BIRD evidence. Each BIRD evidence string is decomposed into the L1 (business-layer) nodes of the joint schema+knowledge graph. v2 (2026-05-20) adds: ColumnAlias node type for column-rename / multi-column-projection evidence, optional 'value' field on grounding_item so Formula expressions can self-ground value literals, and Formula.depends_on edge so joint retrieval can co-fetch dependent Rules / Formulas. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-20-schema-v2-typed-node-extension-design.md and annotation/PILOT_FINDINGS.md for rationale.

record.description: One record per BIRD evidence item.

fields.question: str -- BIRD question (informational only)
fields.raw_evidence: str -- the original BIRD evidence, verbatim
fields.nodes: list[node] -- the typed nodes this evidence decomposes into (may be empty before annotation)
fields.notes: str -- annotator notes. IMPORTANT: record here any evidence that does NOT fit the five node types cleanly -- that feedback is the deliverable of the pilot.

Concept.description: A named business term (e.g. 'high-value customer'). Usually operationalized by a Formula/Rule/ValueMap/ColumnAlias node via the 'defined_by' edge.

fields.id: str -- unique within the record, e.g. 'c1'
fields.name: str -- the business term
fields.definition: str -- optional free-text gloss. Prefer a defined_by edge to a structured node over free text where one fits.
fields.defined_by: str -- optional; id of the Formula/Rule/ValueMap/ColumnAlias node that operationalizes this concept

Formula.description: A computation or derivation expressed over columns. May reference value literals via grounding entries that include a 'value' field, and may depend on sibling Rule / Formula / ValueMap / ColumnAlias nodes via 'depends_on'.

fields.name: str -- name of the computed quantity
fields.expression: str -- the formula, verbatim or lightly normalized
fields.grounding: list[grounding_item] -- maps each term in the expression to a physical column (and optionally a specific value of that column)
fields.depends_on: list[str] -- optional; ids of sibling nodes (Rule / Formula / ValueMap / ColumnAlias) that this Formula's correct interpretation requires. Joint retrieval must co-fetch these.

ValueMap.description: A natural-language label that corresponds to a specific value of a specific column.

fields.name: str -- the natural-language label
fields.value: str -- the column value the label maps to

Rule.description: A filter condition or business convention that is not a single arithmetic formula (e.g. 'churned = no login for 30 days', a fiscal-year convention).

fields.name: str -- optional short name
fields.condition: str -- the predicate / convention, verbatim or lightly normalized

ColumnAlias.description: v2 (2026-05-20). A user-facing term that maps to one or more physical columns. Use for column-rename evidence ('X refers to col_name') and multi-column projections ('hometown refers to city, county, state'). Length-1 bindings cover the single-column case; length>=2 bindings cover column tuples.

fields.name: str -- the user-facing term
fields.bindings: list[{table, column}] -- non-empty. Each entry has 'table' and 'column'.

grounding_item.description: An L1->L2 link: a term used in a Formula/Rule mapped to a physical column (and optionally to a specific value of that column). Use the database schema DDL (embedded in to_annotate.json under 'schemas') to find the table/column. CONSUMPTION RULE when both bare-column entries {term, table, column} and value-bearing entries {term, table, column, value} exist for the same (table, column) on one node: the value-bearing entries together describe filter predicates (WHERE col = value [OR col = value2 ...]); the bare-column entry describes the column's role outside any filter (SELECT, GROUP BY, projection). SQL generators should treat them accordingly.

fields.term: str -- the term as written in the expression/condition
fields.value: str -- OPTIONAL (v2). When present, the term grounds to this column WITH this specific value (e.g. 'carcinogenic' -> molecule.label = '+'). When absent, semantics is v1: term grounds to the column itself. CONVENTION FOR 'term' WHEN value IS PRESENT: prefer the human-readable concept/label as it appears in the user-facing question (e.g. term='carcinogenic'); the raw literal (e.g. term='+') is also acceptable when no distinct human label exists. The 'value' field is authoritative for filter semantics; the 'term' field is for surface-form matching during retrieval.

edges.defined_by: Concept -> {Formula | Rule | ValueMap | ColumnAlias}, referenced by node id within the same record. v2: ColumnAlias added to the legal target set.
edges.depends_on: Formula -> list[{Rule | Formula | ValueMap | ColumnAlias}]. v2 addition. Joint-retrieval semantics: retrieving the Formula must also retrieve every node listed here.

examples._comment: Formula: one evidence -> one Formula node, terms grounded to columns.
examples.raw_evidence: Eligible free rate for K-12 = `Free Meal Count (K-12)` / `Enrollment (K-12)`

examples._comment: ValueMap: a label maps to one value of one column.
Concept + Rule: one evidence -> two nodes joined by a defined_by edge.
examples.raw_evidence: abnormal white blood cell count refers to WBC < 3.5 or WBC > 9.0
examples.notes: One evidence string can decompose into multiple nodes joined by edges.

examples.raw_evidence: magic card market name refers to mcmName

examples._comment: v2: ColumnAlias multi-binding (column tuple) + Formula with grounding.value and depends_on.
examples.raw_evidence: hometown refers to city, county, state; race completion rate from 2007 to 2009 = COUNT(driverId where time is not null) / COUNT(driverId) where year between 2007 and 2009

nodes.name: race completion percentage
nodes.expression: COUNT(driverId WHERE time IS NOT NULL AND year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009) / COUNT(driverId WHERE year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009) * 100

examples.notes: v2 example: multi-binding ColumnAlias and Formula with depends_on. The depends_on list makes the Rule dependencies retrievable alongside the Formula.
